observations.claim: Declarations run at about 40 a week, 25 minutes for a straightforward one, typed into the customs platform from the customer's documents (self reported).
observations.quote: Twenty-five minutes for a straightforward one, and we do about 40 a week.

observations.claim: About 1 declaration in 5 bounces on customer paperwork mismatches, costing about 15 minutes of rework plus a wait of up to a day (self reported).
observations.quote: About 1 in 5 declarations bounces because something on the customer's invoice doesn't add up

observations.claim: The failing checks are mechanical (totals match, origin stated, description recognisable) and could run when documents land at the booking desk.
observations.quote: The checks are mechanical, does the total match, is the origin stated, is the description one of the ones we've seen before.
observations.stated_dependencies: If the booking desk had a checklist run against the documents when they land, I'd get clean files.

observations.claim: A bounced declaration usually lands while the consignment is already moving, turning it into an emergency.
observations.quote: when a declaration bounces, the consignment is usually already rolling

observations.claim: A live in-session demo of the mechanical checks caught a weight mismatch; the clerk's condition for trusting it is that it is right every time, because a wrong all-clear is worse than no check (consultant-led session; the demo is the consultant's work, the condition is the clerk's evidence).
observations.quote: A wrong all-clear is worse than no check.
